rules.catchability: throw participates in ordinary try/catch; uncaught throw becomes raise, then panic if unrecovered under the language effect rules
rules.trap: trap on a throwing numeric operation converts the language effect to Result/Option according to the callable contract
rules.checked_result_apis: APIs named *_checked or explicitly declared Result-returning numeric conversions report expected numeric-domain failures as Err and do not additionally throw those same expected failures
rules.host_failures: ArithmeticException, OverflowException, C++ runtime_error, process signals and Wasm traps are backend implementation evidence only and are never guest Error identity

applies_to: integer remainder/division domains that define zero-divisor failure
exact numeric conversions that would lose information
explicit rounded conversion outside finite target range

NumericResourceError.default_effect: Result.Err or throw only when the invoked API is not Result-returning

applies_to: Decimal.divide_exact when the exact quotient has no terminating base-10 expansion

actor_semantics.throw_inside_actor: catchable by the actor's current try/catch; if uncaught follows throw->raise->panic escalation
actor_semantics.panic_interception: numeric code does not create a special panic path; an actor cannot intercept its own eventual panic
actor_semantics.supervisor_notice: only the final panic escalation reaches the supervisor CONTROL path; a host exception/trap is not itself a valid supervisor notice

error_abi_v1.rules: Codes identify Oreslang guest Error kinds across backend effect carriers. A host exception class, signal, trap opcode or diagnostic string is never sufficient identity.
